articles.headline: SpaceX Rally Lifts Valor's Stake to Nearly $97 Billion After 43% Gain
articles.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Antonio Gracias has emerged as one of the biggest winners from SpaceX's (NASDAQ:SPCX) market debut, as Valor Equity Partners' stake in the rocket company was worth almost $97 billion as of Monday's close. The Chicago-based private equity firm's position has helped lift Gracias' estimated net worth to $24.4 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, which is valuing his fortune for the first time. SpaceX shares have gained 43% since trading began in New York on Friday, bringing sharper attention to Gracias' long-running bet on Elon Musk's companies.
Gracias' relationship with Musk stretches back decades and has possibly been central to Valor's access to some of Musk's most valuable ventures. Valor became the first institutional investor in Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) in 2005, invested in SpaceX three years later, and backed Neuralink and the Boring Co. Gracias also extended Musk a short-term loan in 2008 when his companies were facing bankruptcy, while Musk invested $2 million into each of Valor's first two funds. By the time Gracias left Tesla's board in 2021, he had built a stake currently worth more than $1.6 billion after adjusting for a 2022 stock split.
Valor insiders own about a quarter of the firm's assets under management, but they hold 64% of Valor Space Holdings, which owns a SpaceX position worth about $18.8 billion, according to an April 2026 filing. Bloomberg credits Gracias with a personal SpaceX stake worth $16.8 billion through Valor funds, plus $3.3 billion in non-SpaceX insider assets and a Valor ownership stake worth about $2.7 billion. Valor's SpaceX funds have already recorded more than $39 billion in gains since the start of the year, and future carried interest distributions could possibly add further upside when the funds eventually return capital to investors.

articles.headline: How much money did Elon Musk make in SpaceXs stock market debut?
articles.text:
Elon Musk is now the world's first trillionaire. SpaceX's historic debut on the stock market on Friday launched the CEO to unprecedented levels of wealth; his personal fortune now amounts to $1.1tn, an increase of more than $62bn since the previous day, according to Forbes.
The rocket, satellite and AI company raised $75bn from its record-breaking initial public offering (IPO), and is now valued at $2.1tn after its first day of public trading.
Musk was already the world's wealthiest person. In the days before SpaceX officially went public, his net worth hit $782bn, dropping by $50bn in one month due to a decline in Tesla's share price, according to Forbes. However, the figure represents a huge leap from a decade ago, when the tech executive's net worth hovered around $14bn – and an even bigger jump compared with 15 years earlier, when he was worth just $680m, according to Forbes.
It can be hard to conceptualize such exorbitant wealth. To drive home just how much money $1.1tn is: only about 21 countries' yearly economic output exceeds $1tn. Even Musk's birthplace isn't part of that elite club; South Africa's output of goods and service is closer to $480bn. A trillion dollars is enough to buy 243bn gallons of gasoline. (That's more than the nearly 137bn gallons Americans used last year.)
SpaceX's stock soared after its debut. At market close, at 4pm ET, its share price was $161, up 19% from its initial price of $135 per share. SpaceX had opened at $150 a share before peaking at $176 at midday.
The vast majority of Musk's money is tied up in stocks and equity, and isn't available as cash he can quickly spend. His portfolio of companies includes Tesla, the electric car maker, and xAI, the AI startup that was folded into SpaceX earlier this year.
Musk's fortune is unprecedented, not just for its size but the speed at which it grew.
